subject.title: fix(agents): finalize killed subagent task rows via maintenance to avoid kill-vs-complete race

question: Should this older lost-to-succeeded maintenance design be retired, or rebased into the current provisional-kill task-owner architecture only for historical cleanup?
rationale: The current branch conflicts with main and overlaps a merged session-state redesign; automation should not choose the terminal-state model for maintainers.

options.title: Rebase Narrow Cleanup
options.body: Port only the remaining historical terminal-run maintenance repair and remove the obsolete lost-to-succeeded override so current provisional-kill semantics stay authoritative.

options.title: Close As Superseded
options.body: Treat the merged current-main reconciliation work and narrower follow-ups as the path forward, and close this stale conflicting branch by maintainer choice.

options.title: Accept The Older Model
options.body: Keep the maintenance-lost design, but maintainers would need to explicitly own the session-state semantics conflict and refresh proof after rebase.

recommendation.title: Rebase Narrow Cleanup
recommendation.body: Port only the remaining historical terminal-run maintenance repair and remove the obsolete lost-to-succeeded override so current provisional-kill semantics stay authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current-main architecture this branch now overlaps, so he is the best available owner for the terminal-state tradeoff.
